column2: in `review_tally.py`, `_record_classification_and_ledger` / `_ledger_entry` run with `outcome="oos" if is_oos else result` before the finding artifact branch where neutral rescue is applied. `_ledger_entry` only upgrades latent body severity to `oos` and has no voter-severity / neutral-rescue input. a rescued 1-yes high-severity neutral can therefore record `outcome=neutral` (or otherwise drift) in `findings-ledger.tsv` while `oos.md` and kv counts say oos, failing planned regression assertions and reproducing the plan’s ledger-drift failure mode.

`_write_findings_ledger` in `plan_review_tally.py` only calls `_tally_votes_for_id` (yes/no/result) and mirrors latent via body regex; it never reads per-voter `severity=` values. the plan requires rescued neutrals to record ledger `outcome="oos"`, but without severities the shared rescue helper cannot run there. plan-review parity with code-review breaks and the oos audit trail stays incomplete.

without an explicit rescued-to-oos branch before the generic rejected/neutral fallback, high-severity single-yes neutrals still flow through the rejected path: they land in `rejected-findings.md`, increment `neutral_count` / `rejected_count`, and `oos_rejected_count` stays 0. the plan’s rescued `elif` must mirror latent reroute side effects (`oos_rejected` increment, `oos.md` append with `result=neutral (neutral-rescued)`, `_record_tally`) and sit after latent reroute and before the rejected fallback to avoid double-routing.

the code-review rescue flow stops at aggregate kvs and direct file routing; `_record_tally` still emits `outcome=rejected` for non-accepted items (including rescued neutrals), and `emit-tally` rebuilds `rejected-findings.md` / `review-summary.json` from those rows. rescued in-scope findings therefore reappear as rejected downstream and the oos rescue is lost.
